date.as_written: śaileṣu śailendu samāsame śake[1757] raṣasya (!) śubhrārddha†padākahā† ravau | strībhe gate rke

notes: The chronogram śaila (7) iṣu (5) śaila (7) indu (1), read right to left, gives 1757. The era is stated as śake, so this is Śaka 1757, about 1835 CE. The catalogue's 'SAM 1757' is only a label; if it were Vikrama the date would be about 1700 CE, but the text says śake. 'raṣasya (!)' is a corrupt month name. The best guess is iṣasya (Iṣa = Āśvina), which agrees with 'strībhe gate 'rke' (the sun having entered Virgo/Kanyā); sahasya (Pauṣa) is less likely. 'śubhrārddha' = the bright half (śukla); the tithi in '†padākahā†' is corrupt (perhaps pratipadā?). ravau = Sunday. The scribe's name is corrupt in '’do lālaratnākaravi dvide ’likhat'. One possible reading is lālaratnākara-vid/vidvān; the catalogue gives Ratnākaralāla. Paśupeśadeśa = 'the land of the Lord Paśupati', i.e. Nepal (Kathmandu Valley). It is the place of copying, not explicitly the scribe's residence.
